answer: Each identity drives one jetty pile into a canyon inlet, posts a 70-credit bond, and files it in the atlas register. Each epoch the canyon current scours the pile base, and an auditor re-measures scour depth against the atlas sounding table: depth outside range, a reused serial, or a missing jetty log burns the bond. The pile fee starts at 27, up 9 per queued pile: the kth fake pays 27+9(k-1), the 1000th 9018, and 1000 fakes 4,522,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-pile ring fails: one pile cannot back two identities, so a second filing burns both bonds. Honest identities pay 27 once.
